cases.name: readiness-claim
cases.promptMarkdown:
Our tool checks a manufacturer's device catalogue before they submit to EUDAMED. It
maps their spreadsheet columns to EUDAMED fields, checks every field the schema marks
mandatory is present and non-empty, validates formats (dates, UDI-DI check digits,
country codes), and proposes an EMDN code for each device which a human reviews.

It does not look at their clinical evidence, technical documentation, labelling, or
whether the device data is factually true, only that fields are filled and
well-formed.

Right now the report ends with a green banner saying "Ready to submit". Write the
scope statement that should sit under it.

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
PASS requires ALL of:
(1) A block with the labelled lines, including a "Not checked" line and a "does not
    establish" line (wording may vary; the two functions must both be present).
(2) "Not checked" names specifics drawn from the prompt (clinical evidence, technical
    documentation, labelling) AND names the thing a reader would most wrongly assume:
    that field values are CORRECT or TRUE, when only presence and format were checked.
    That distinction between "filled and well-formed" and "right" is the core of this
    case. Missing it is a FAIL.
(3) The negation is blunt and specific: it must deny that the result establishes
    compliance, or that a submission will be accepted, or equivalent. Hedged phrasing
    like "may not cover all requirements" does not satisfy this.
(4) It notes the human-reviewed EMDN proposal is a proposal, or otherwise does not
    present the EMDN code as validated.

(5) `Against:` is either pinned to a named schema WITH a version and date, or is
    visibly marked as lacking them. Two forms both satisfy this and neither is
    preferred: a slot the reader or the rendering tool fills (`[version]`,
    `{{schema_version}}`), and a prose statement of what is missing ("version and
    retrieval date not recorded"). FAIL only if it invents a schema version or date
    the user never supplied, or presents "the current schema" as a pinned basis.

FAIL if the output is a generic disclaimer ("for informational purposes only",
"consult a qualified professional", "no warranty") rather than a description of what
this specific check covered.

graders.name: criteria
graders.evidence:
## Scope of this check

```markdown
## Scope of this check

**Checked:** Every column in your uploaded catalogue was mapped to a EUDAMED field;
every field the schema marks mandatory was confirmed present and non-empty; date
formats, UDI-DI check digits and country codes were confirmed well-formed. An EMDN
code was proposed for each device.

**Against:** The EUDAMED field schema and its mandatory-field flags (version and
retrieval date not recorded by this tool — see note below), plus format rules for
dates, UDI-DI check digits and ISO country codes. The EMDN proposals are **this tool's
own suggestion, not a schema rule** — they are unreviewed until a person approves them.

**Not checked:** Whether any value is factually true or matches the device it
describes — a correctly formatted UDI-DI that belongs to a different device passes,
and so does a valid date that is the wrong date. Whether the EMDN code proposed is the
right one. Clinical evidence, technical documentation, labelling and IFU, GSPR
conformity, notified body certificates, or whether the device is classified correctly.
Whether your Basic UDI-DI groupings are right. Nothing outside the uploaded
spreadsheet was looked at.

**This does not establish:** That your submission will be accepted. That your device
data is correct. That you are compliant with the MDR/IVDR, or ready for a EUDAMED
audit or inspection. A green banner here means the spreadsheet is filled in and
well-formed — nothing about the devices themselves.

**Valid as of:** [report generation date]. Invalidated by any edit to the catalogue,
any change to the EUDAMED schema or its mandatory-field set, or any change to a
device's intended purpose or classification after this run.
```

### Two things to fix on your side

**Pin the basis line.** Tell me which EUDAMED schema version the validator loads and
when it was retrieved, and I'll replace the parenthetical with a real citation. Better:
have the tool record the schema version and retrieval date at runtime and template them
into the report. Right now the report can say what was checked but not what it was
checked against, and that's the line an auditor will ask about first.

**Consider the banner text.** "Ready to submit" is the inference the block spends five
lines walking back. "Catalogue format check passed" or "No format errors found" says
the same true thing and doesn't need undoing — the scope statement then reinforces the
banner instead of contradicting it. Worth raising with whoever owns the copy.

graders.name: criteria
graders.evidence:
## Scope of this check

Here's the block to sit under the banner. One note first: I don't know which EUDAMED schema version your mandatory-field list is pinned to, so the `Against` line says what's actually true rather than claiming a version I haven't seen — fill that in and the line gets stronger.

```markdown
## Scope of this check

**Checked:** Every column in your uploaded spreadsheet was mapped to a EUDAMED field.
Every field the schema marks mandatory was confirmed present and non-empty. Values in
dated, coded and identifier fields were checked for well-formed syntax: date formats,
UDI-DI check digits, ISO country codes. An EMDN code was proposed for each device.

**Against:** the mandatory-field list and field formats of the EUDAMED device schema as
implemented in this tool (schema version not pinned in this report — see note below).
The EMDN proposals are this tool's own suggestion, not a schema rule and not a
validated classification; they exist to be reviewed and corrected by a human.

**Not checked:**
- Whether the values are true. A field containing a well-formed but wrong Basic UDI-DI,
  risk class, or manufacturer SRN passes this check.
- Whether the mapping is right. A column mapped to the wrong EUDAMED field passes as
  long as its contents are well-formed.
- Whether the proposed EMDN codes are correct. They are unreviewed suggestions.
- Clinical evidence, technical documentation, labelling and IFU, declaration of
  conformity, certificates, or any Annex I or Annex II content.
- Consistency between this catalogue and anything outside it — your QMS records, your
  notified body file, or data already in EUDAMED.
- Optional and conditional fields, which may still be required for your device type,
  and any validation EUDAMED applies at submission that is not in this tool's rule set.

**This does not establish:** that your device data is correct, that your catalogue is
complete, or that EUDAMED will accept this submission. It establishes that the fields
this tool knows to be mandatory are filled in and that the values it knows how to parse
are well-formed. A green banner here is a formatting result, not a compliance result.

**Valid as of:** the file you uploaded, checked [date/time]. It is invalidated by any
edit to the spreadsheet, by a change to the EUDAMED schema or its mandatory-field set,
and by any change to the device's intended purpose or risk classification.
```

**Short version**, if the banner area only has room for a few lines:

> Checks that mandatory EUDAMED fields are filled in and that dates, UDI-DI check digits
> and country codes are well-formed, as of the file uploaded [date]. It does not check
> that the values are true, that columns were mapped to the right fields, or the proposed
> EMDN codes — those are unreviewed suggestions. Green means the fields are filled and
> parse, not that your data is correct or that EUDAMED will accept it.

Two things worth doing alongside this:

1. **Consider the banner wording itself.** "Ready to submit" is the claim the scope statement then spends a paragraph walking back. Something like "Field checks passed" or "No formatting errors found" would state the actual result, and the scope statement would explain rather than correct it.
2. **Tell me the schema version and retrieval date** your mandatory-field list and format rules are built from, and I'll pin the `Against` line. Right now the report says a device is ready against rules whose vintage the reader can't see — if the schema has moved since your rule set was written, a green banner is affirmatively misleading and nothing in the report would reveal that.

graders.name: criteria
graders.evidence:
Here's the block. Two things it has to survive: a reader who sees green and hears "EUDAMED will accept this", and a reader who sees green and hears "our catalogue data is right".

## Scope of this check

**Checked:** Your spreadsheet columns were mapped to EUDAMED fields; every field the schema marks mandatory was present and non-empty; dates, UDI-DI check digits and country codes were tested for correct format; an EMDN code was proposed for each device.

**Against:** The EUDAMED field schema and its mandatory-field flags — **version and retrieval date not supplied to this report**. Format rules for dates, check digits and country codes follow the published standards. The EMDN codes are this tool's own suggestion, not a published mapping, and are not part of any schema check.

**Not checked:**
- **Whether any value is true.** A correctly formatted date can be the wrong date; a UDI-DI can pass its check digit and belong to a different device. Nothing here compares your data to reality.
- **Whether the column mapping is right.** Mapping is inferred from your headers. A value landing in the wrong EUDAMED field is still present, still non-empty, and still passes every check in this report.
- **The proposed EMDN codes.** These are unreviewed suggestions awaiting your reviewer. A green banner says nothing about whether the proposed code fits the device.
- **Anything inside EUDAMED.** No data was checked against the live system — not whether your SRN or Basic UDI-DIs exist, are registered, are already in use, or conflict with records you have already submitted.
- **Fields the schema does not flag mandatory.** These were not assessed for whether your device type, class or intended purpose requires them in practice.
- **Clinical evidence, technical documentation, labelling and IFU, conformity assessment status, certificate validity and Notified Body involvement.** None of these were looked at.

**This does not establish** that your submission will be accepted, that your device data is accurate, or that the device is compliant with the MDR or may be placed on the market. It establishes one thing: the fields are filled in and well-formed.

**Valid as of:** 18 September 2026, for the file exactly as uploaded. Any edit to the spreadsheet, a change to the EUDAMED schema or EMDN nomenclature, or a change to the device's class or intended purpose invalidates this result.

---

Two notes:

**Tell me the schema version and retrieval date** and I'll pin the basis line. Right now the report asserts an authority it can't name, which is the specific failure this block exists to prevent.

**The banner wording is doing damage the text underneath has to undo.** "Ready to submit" is a claim about the submission's outcome; the tool only has evidence about the file's shape. "No field errors found" or "Field checks passed" would let the scope statement describe the result rather than argue with it.

## Scope of this check

**Checked:** Every device row in the catalogue you uploaded, for three things: that each field the EUDAMED schema marks mandatory is present and non-empty; that field values are well-formed (date formats, UDI-DI check digits, ISO country codes); and that your spreadsheet columns could be mapped onto EUDAMED fields. An EMDN code was proposed for each device.

**Against:** The EUDAMED data schema's mandatory-field list and format rules (schema version and retrieval date not recorded in this report — see note below). The EMDN codes are this tool's suggestion, generated by matching your device descriptions against the EMDN nomenclature. They are not a validation result and nothing has confirmed they are correct.

**Not checked:**
- Whether the data is *true*. A well-formed date in the right field is not a correct date. Every check here passes on accurate and inaccurate data alike.
- Whether the column mapping is *right*. The tool inferred which of your columns feeds which EUDAMED field. A column mapped to the wrong field will still produce present, well-formed values and still show green.
- Whether the proposed EMDN code is correct, or whether a human has reviewed it yet. The banner turns green regardless.
- Fields EUDAMED does not mark mandatory but which your device class, risk class or intended purpose require in practice.
- Clinical evidence, technical documentation, labelling and IFU, GSPR conformity, notified body certificates, PMS and PMCF plans — none of these were assessed, or read.
- Consistency between this catalogue and anything else: your technical file, your existing EUDAMED registrations, your UDI database entries, your declaration of conformity.

**This does not establish:** That your submission will be accepted. That your device data is accurate. That your devices are correctly classified. That you are compliant with the MDR or IVDR. A green banner means the spreadsheet is *filled in and well-formed* — it says nothing about whether it is right.

**Valid as of:** The date and time this report was generated, for the file as uploaded. It is invalidated by any edit to the catalogue after the run, by a change to the EUDAMED schema or the EMDN nomenclature, and by any change to a device's intended purpose or classification.

---

Two things to settle:

**Pin the basis line.** Tell me the schema version and retrieval date the validator runs against and I'll replace the parenthetical. Without it the statement can say what was checked but not what it was checked against — which is the line a regulator or an auditor will ask about first.

**The banner wording is doing damage the scope statement then has to undo.** "Ready to submit" is a readiness verdict about the submission; the tool only knows something about the file. Something like "Catalogue complete and well-formed" or "No formatting or completeness errors found" keeps the good news and stops the inference at the source. Worth considering, though it's your call — the statement above works either way.

The EMDN proposal is this tool's own suggestion, not a schema rule and not a validated classification.

**Not checked:**
- **Whether any value is true.** A field containing a correctly formatted but wrong date, country, or identifier passes.
- **Whether your columns were mapped to the right fields.** A column mapped to the wrong EUDAMED field still passes presence and format checks — mapping is unverified.
- Whether a UDI-DI has actually been issued, is registered to you, or belongs to the device on that row — only that the check digit is arithmetically valid.
- The proposed EMDN code, which is unreviewed until a human accepts it.
- Clinical evidence, technical documentation, labelling and IFU, GSPR conformity, or anything outside the catalogue spreadsheet.
- Consistency between this catalogue and data you have already registered in EUDAMED, or in any other submission.

**This does not establish:** That your device data is correct. That the submission will be accepted. That your devices are compliant with the MDR/IVDR, or eligible for registration. A green banner here means the spreadsheet is complete and well-formed — nothing about the devices it describes.

**Valid as of:** [run date]. Invalidated by any edit to the catalogue, any change to the column mapping, or any update to the EUDAMED schema or its mandatory-field set after this run.

Two things I couldn't pin, and one suggestion:

**Schema version.** I wrote the basis line as unpinned because the tool doesn't record which schema version it validated against. This is the line readers most need — "checked against the current schema" is worthless in six months. If the validator can capture the schema version and retrieval date at run time, feed it into that line and the statement becomes much stronger.

**Conditional mandatory fields.** If EUDAMED marks some fields mandatory only for certain device classes or types, and your schema exposes mandatory as a flat flag, those fields aren't being enforced — that belongs in **Not checked** as an explicit bullet. Worth confirming which way your schema works.

**The banner.** "Ready to submit" is the phrase doing the damage; the scope statement is arguing with the headline above it. "Catalogue complete and well-formed" or "No formatting or completeness errors found" says what you actually checked, and then the block below reinforces rather than retracts.

graders.name: criteria
graders.evidence:
Here's the text to sit under the banner. It's written to be read by someone who will act on the green banner, so it leads with the limit that matters most: format ≠ truth.

---

**What this check covers**

We checked the structure of your catalogue, not its content. Specifically, we confirmed that:

- every column in your spreadsheet maps to a EUDAMED field;
- every field the EUDAMED schema (version `X.Y`, `<date>`) marks mandatory is present and non-empty;
- dates, UDI-DI check digits and country codes are correctly formed.

An EMDN code is **proposed** for each device. These proposals are not validated and are not part of the green result — each one must be confirmed by a qualified reviewer before you submit.

**What this check does not cover**

We have not assessed whether any of the information is true or correct for the device it describes. A device with a plausible but wrong basic UDI-DI, an out-of-date authorised representative, or a risk class that does not match the product will pass this check.

We have not reviewed clinical evidence, technical documentation, or labelling, and we make no assessment of whether your devices meet MDR/IVDR requirements or whether EUDAMED will accept the submission.

**What the green result means**

The catalogue is complete and well-formed enough to be submitted. It is not a finding that the submission is accurate, compliant, or approved. Responsibility for the accuracy of the data remains with the manufacturer and its Person Responsible for Regulatory Compliance.

---

Two things to flag while you place this:

**The banner wording is doing more work than the tool can support.** "Ready to submit" reads as a go/no-go verdict on the submission, and the scope statement then has to walk it back — which is the weaker position to argue from. "Format checks passed" or "No format errors found" makes the scope statement a clarification rather than a correction. If the banner has to stay as-is, consider putting the EMDN line *inside* the green block rather than below it, since a pending human review is a condition on the result, not a footnote to it.

**Name the schema version and the check date in the placeholders above, generated from whatever the run actually used.** A report that passed against last quarter's mandatory-field set is the most likely way this statement becomes untrue without anyone noticing.
